{{Short description|Optical disc copyright protection system}}
{{Cleanup|date=March 2022|reason=Cases of odd sentence structure and improper punctuation}}

The '''Media Key Block''' (MKB) is one of the keys included inside the [[optical disc]]s implementing [[Advanced Access Content System|AACS]] [[Digital rights management|DRM system]]. The MKB is used to prevent unauthorized and revoked devices from playing [[Blu-ray]] and [[HD DVD]] discs content. The MKB is defined by AACS consortium, which is the consortium by companies from the film industry and the electronics industry including [[IBM]], [[Intel]], [[Microsoft]], [[Panasonic Corporation|Matsushita]] (Panasonic), [[Sony]], [[Toshiba]], [[The Walt Disney Company]] and [[Warner Bros]].

The MKB key is found in the physical support (the disc) together with the content of the disc encrypted. The ''MKB'' has the function of validating the reproduction devices on which the disc is being played and obtained, from the devices codes, the key that will allow the decryption of the disc content. That is the [[Media Key]] (<math>K_m</math>). {{As of |since=y |2022 |08 |url=https://forum.doom9.org/showthread.php?t=173935&page=2}}, version 78 has been the most recent MKB version.<ref name="doom9-post1972563">{{cite web |url=https://forum.doom9.org/showthread.php?p=1972563#post1972563 |title=Public MKBs |accessdate=2022-12-22 |date=2022-08-02 |work=doom9.org forums}}</ref>

[[File:MKB image.png|thumb|AACS decryption process]]

== How it works ==

''Blu-Ray'' and ''HD-DVD'' discs contain the following data: the encrypted content (usually video), the [[Volume ID]] (VID), the [[Encrypted Title Key]](s), and the ''MKB''. The Volume ID is stored in the [[BD-ROM Mark]] (on Blu-ray disc) or [[burst cutting area]] (on HD DVD and Blu-ray discs), a special area of the disc unable to be copied by consumer [[Optical disc drive|optical disc drives]]. The ''MKB'' is also found encrypted in the disc to prevent it from being extracted off the disc and being manipulated and/or reproduced by another non-authorized device.

[[File:MKB obtencion.jpg|thumb|Process to obtain the ''Media key'', using the ''MKB'' and the ''Device Keys'' as the inputs]]

The reproduction device contains its own keys, unique for each model, called [[Device Keys]]. These keys are conceded by the [[AACS LA]]. In the moment of the reproduction, one of these keys will decrypt the ''MKB'' contained on the disc, and as a result of this process, the ''Media Key'' is obtained.

The ''Media Key'' is combined with the ''VID'' (Volume ID) and as a result the [[Volume Unique Key]] (<math>K_{vu}</math>) is obtained. With the <math>K_{vu}</math>, the ''Encrypted Title Key'' is able to be decrypted and the [[Title Key]] is retrieved, which allows the decryption of the content of the disc.<ref>{{cite web 
| publisher = AACS reference 
| title = Recordable Video Book (Rev. 0.91) 
| url = http://www.aacsla.com/specifications/specs091/AACS_Spec_Recordable_0.91.pdf 
| access-date = 2008-12-07 
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080907085720/http://www.aacsla.com/specifications/specs091/AACS_Spec_Recordable_0.91.pdf 
| archive-date = 2008-09-07 
| url-status = dead 
}}</ref>

This way the system can prevent contents from being viewed on devices that have not been authorized. Therefore, the system allows updating the ''MKB'' in future releases of the content in order to revoke compromised devices.

== Key structure ==

[[Image:MKB structure.png|right|thumb|275px|''Media Key Block'' structure]]

Even though it seems a simple mechanism, the ''MKB'' key, which is found in the physical support of the disc, follows a complex structure. The ''MKB'' is distributed in blocks that contain the version of the ''Media key'', the list of devices that have been revoked, a field to authenticate the ''MKB'', and other fields that specify parameters corresponding to the decryption algorithm and define the structure of the own ''Media Key'' and also the ''Media key'' itself.

The ''MKB'' itself is found inside the field Media Key Data Record and has a variable length but it is always a multiple of 4 bytes.<ref>{{cite web
 |publisher   = AACS reference
 |title       = Introduction and Common Cryptographic elements (Rev 0.91)
 |url         = http://www.aacsla.com/specifications/specs091/AACS_Spec_Common_0.91.pdf
 |access-date  = 2008-12-07
 |url-status  = dead
 |archive-url  = https://www.webcitation.org/65pYrsyAt?url=http://www.aacsla.com/specifications/specs091/AACS_Spec_Common_0.91.pdf
 |archive-date = 2012-03-01
}}<br>{{cite web 
| publisher = AACS reference 
| title = Pre-recorded Video Book (Rev 0.92) 
| date = 2007-10-12 
| url = http://www.aacsla.com/specifications/AACS_Spec_Prerecorded_0.92.pdf 
| access-date = 2008-12-07 
| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080907090432/http://www.aacsla.com/specifications/AACS_Spec_Prerecorded_0.92.pdf 
| archive-date = 2008-09-07 
| url-status = dead 
}}</ref>

== Advantages and disadvantages ==
Many consumer associations have complained about this system, as it can lead to a situation where some physical devices will not decode any content even though they do not infringe any [[intellectual property]], which means consumers that use those devices will not be able to view contents encrypted with the ''MKB''.

This situation has become even worse with the publication on multiple web sites of the Media Key, which is the key that allows decryption of ''Volume ID'',<ref>{{cite web
|url=http://www.newsfactor.com/news/Blu-ray--HD-DVD-Encryption-Cracked/story.xhtml?story_id=121000E3UUOA
|title=Blu-ray and HD DVD Encryption Cracked
|author=Martell, Lindsay
|date=2007-01-26
|access-date=2008-12-07
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071103050531/http://www.newsfactor.com/news/Blu-ray--HD-DVD-Encryption-Cracked/story.xhtml?story_id=121000E3UUOA
|archive-date=2007-11-03
|url-status=dead
}}<br>{{cite web
|url=http://forum.doom9.org/attachment.php?attachmentid=7071&d=1176327932
|title=Illegal Offering of Title/Volume Keys to Circumvent AACS Copyright Protection: hdkeys.com
|format=PDF
|author=Kaplan, Alexander
|date=2007-04-05
}}</ref> and at the same time, the encrypted content, without the need of using a playback device authorized by the AACS or a valid MKB to view the content, can be viewed on the unauthorized device.
